headline: Navajo County land due diligence: flood, soil, and elevation from free public data
metaDescription: What the free government data shows for Navajo County, Arizona — FEMA flood-zone read, dominant SSURGO soils, and elevation band for land investors, with named sources.
intro: Before you buy vacant land in Navajo County, three free federal datasets tell you most of what kills a resale: the FEMA flood zone, the dominant soil order (which drives septic feasibility), and the elevation band. AcreOS runs all three on every parcel — here is the county-level read, with sources.

dataSnapshot.scope: Navajo County reference read, sampled at the county centroid from the same free federal datasets AcreOS runs on every parcel

figures.label: Elevation band
figures.value: High plateau, dropping at the Mogollon Rim
figures.note: Navajo County runs from high Colorado Plateau down across the Mogollon Rim — elevation and access swing widely, and many cheap parcels are pre-1976 wildcat splits with no recorded road easement.
figures.source: USGS — Elevations and Distances in the United States

figures.label: Dominant soil orders (SSURGO)
figures.note: Northern Arizona's arid-zone orders mean thin, low-organic soils; septic feasibility and water access are the buyer's diligence cost on un-permitted parcels.
figures.source: USDA NRCS — The Twelve Orders of Soil Taxonomy

figures.label: Flood-risk read
figures.note: Flood risk concentrates in FEMA-mapped washes and the Little Colorado drainage; pull the parcel's NFHL zone before you buy.

dataSnapshot.disclaimer: Figures are a Navajo County reference read from public federal datasets and do not replace a parcel-level lookup. Coverage and currency vary by county GIS; always pull the parcel's own FEMA NFHL zone, SSURGO map unit, and 3DEP elevation before relying on these.

faq.q: Is land in Navajo County in a flood zone?
faq.a: It depends on the parcel. Flood risk concentrates in FEMA-mapped washes and the Little Colorado drainage; pull the parcel's NFHL zone before you buy. The only reliable answer is the parcel's own FEMA NFHL zone, which the free AcreOS parcel check pulls in seconds.

faq.q: What kind of soil does Navajo County have?
faq.a: Northern Arizona's arid-zone orders mean thin, low-organic soils; septic feasibility and water access are the buyer's diligence cost on un-permitted parcels. For a specific parcel, the SSURGO map unit gives you the exact soil series and its septic-suitability rating.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for data to do diligence in Navajo County?
faq.a: No. The flood, soil, and elevation reads above come from free federal datasets (FEMA, USDA NRCS, USGS). AcreOS runs them on every parcel at no cost; you only reach for paid data providers once your deal volume earns it.
